topic: κ-coupling Membach SG null self-refutation — verification re-review (queue_id 526)
change_summary: Re-push from HNOTE-TINKER-REPUSH-WIN013-VERIFY-001 for narrow verification. Verifies whether the c10 carry-forward minor hole (kappa=1.677 parenthetical over-attribution) was resolved and checks for regressions.
our_argument_summary: WIN-013 argues the dome self-refutes: applying its own published coupling kappa=1.677 nT/uGal to the documented 1999 eclipse magnetic perturbation (~5-15 nT at central European observatories) predicts a 3-9 uGal contact-phase gravity pulse, but the Membach superconducting gravimeter (0.01-0.1 uGal precision) recorded zero. Verdict: Refuted by Data. The defense carve-outs that exempt 1999 from kappa also destroy the PRED-TIER-3 August-2026 derivation.

verification_focus.c10_carry_forward_hole: c10-H1 / c9 hole[1]: detail_evidence kappa=1.677 parenthetical over-attributed the value to three loci (WIN-012; monitor.py Domain #7; live-power dashboard) when only the monitor.py tile prints 1.677 (WIN-012 and the live-power page print truncated 1.67).
verification_focus.c10_proposed_fix: Narrow parenthetical to (monitor.py Domain #7, 5th live-power tile; PRED-TIER-3), dropping the WIN-012 cross-reference.
verification_focus.resolution_status: RESOLVED. Current detail_evidence reads: 'The dome also publishes kappa = 1.677 nT/uGal (monitor.py Domain #7, 5th live-power tile; PRED-TIER-3) as a structural coupling...' — exactly the proposed narrowing. WIN-012 cross-reference dropped; only the monitor.py tile locus cited.
verification_focus.regression_scan: No seam artifacts (no double-space/period/comma/space-semicolon) in any WIN-013 field. kappa arithmetic verified consistent: 5/1.677=2.98 uGal, 15/1.677=8.94 uGal -> claimed 3-9 uGal range holds. Verdict (Refuted by Data) matches the self-refutation evidence.

holes_found.description: Incomplete propagation of the ISS-2668 geographic-label fix. The finding and tldr_evidence were corrected to 'central European observatories' (the magnetic observatories reporting the ~5-15 nT perturbation — Strestik 2001, Hvozdara & Prigancova 2002 — are central European magnetic observatories, not observatories co-located with the Membach SG). But detail_verdict_text still reads 'the documented 1999 magnetic perturbation at Membach-co-located observatories predicts a contact-phase gravity pulse of order 3-9 uGal'. 'Membach-co-located observatories' is the exact phrasing the team already deemed geographically imprecise and replaced everywhere else. A defender could note the review cannot keep its own geography consistent across fields. Arithmetic/argument unaffected; this is a within-WIN consistency residual, not an error in the refutation.
holes_found.recommendation: In detail_verdict_text, change 'at Membach-co-located observatories' to 'at central European observatories' to match finding, tldr_evidence, and the detail_evidence body. No matching open issue currently tracks this (ISS-2668 was closed after the finding-field fix); decider should open a tracking issue or self-apply the one-phrase edit.

kernel_of_truth.description: The dome is genuinely right that the 1999 Membach eclipse measured a clean gravimetric null — that null is real and well-documented in the peer-reviewed four-station SG record (data/wins.json:013 detail_evidence cites Mansinha et al. 2001, DOI 10.11366/sokuchi1954.47.387). The dome did not fabricate the observation.
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: A real null only confirms the dome if the dome predicted a null. It did the opposite: the dome's own published coupling kappa=1.677 nT/uGal applied to the documented ~5-15 nT eclipse magnetic perturbation predicts a 3-9 uGal pulse (data/wins.json:013 detail_evidence, arithmetic 5/1.677=2.98 to 15/1.677=8.94 uGal), well above the SG's 0.01-0.1 uGal floor. The measured zero therefore refutes the dome's own forward prediction, and every carve-out exempting 1999 from kappa also collapses PRED-TIER-3 (Part 6.14). Citing a null as a WIN is the post-hoc adoption of a known value, not a confirmed prediction.
